description: Target behaviour, rendered by the reference browser engine: three lines of text whose underlines carry visibly different weights (thin, heavy, and the shorthand form), with the weight changing mid-line from one run of characters to the next.

The same exported markup in a second browser engine: the weights are honoured but the heavy segments are drawn detached and offset above the baseline. This cross-renderer inconsistency is an accepted trade-off, not a defect to correct.
The same exported markup in a third browser engine: weights honoured, decoration lines positioned slightly lower than the reference. Also an accepted trade-off.

The same exported markup in a fourth browser engine, which drops some of the weighted decorations entirely. Accepted renderer limitation — the library's job is to emit the weight, not to compensate for consumers of the markup.

Target canvas render: a single text object carrying all three decoration kinds at once — line above, line through and line below — where each run of characters sets its own decoration weight independently (thin blue runs next to heavy green runs).

Target canvas render with the selection box visible: two lines of text where per-character decoration weight varies across all three decoration kinds. Note the heaviest decorations extending past the object's bounding box — the accepted visual trade-off of the feature.
